title: 1788 Historical Foundation Slice
sourcePaths: source-import/markdown/Crimson Dunes/Jonathan Giya/Working with Indigenous Australians 00aa89833a2d44b2ad54ee81e42394e6.md
purpose: Define the First Fleet / original magical stowaway foundation that creates durable world flags influencing the 1810 playable start.
scopeBoundaries: Preserve source-import material separately; do not overwrite raw source.
All structures in this file are draft until Author Mode promotion.
Indigenous magical systems should be handled through respectful constraints and local knowledge boundaries.
1788 events create foundation flags, not fixed player choices unless later adapted into playable historical encounters.

overview.dateRange: 1788 to early post-arrival period, with consequences extending to 1810
overview.premise: A magical stowaway or hidden magical presence arrives with or around the First Fleet. This presence interprets Australia through British/European wizarding assumptions and begins encountering evidence of local land-based magical systems that do not fit those assumptions.

currentDecisionState.contactStyle: unresolved; indirect investigation is currently safest default until decided
currentDecisionState.linked1810Outcome: Crimson Dunes is locally founded by 1810 but not yet ICW-recognised; direct ICW envoy/correspondence begins soon after.

originalMagicalStowawayProfile.recommendedDefault: one concealed magical stowaway, identity unresolved

identityOptions.label: One concealed stowaway
pros: Easy to tie to guilt, secrecy, discovery, and records
risks: May over-centralise foundation history around one outsider

identityOptions.label: Accidental magical convict
pros: Clear reason to hide and survive
risks: Needs careful handling around coercion and agency

identityOptions.label: Official-but-secret British wizarding observer
risks: Could overemphasise British institutional control too early

identityOptions.label: Small hidden family/group
risks: More complex to validate and canonise

initialCapabilities: Limited knowledge of land-based Australian magic
initialLimitations: Misreads local magic through British categories
Risk of exposing magic among Muggle settlement

magicalContext: International Statute of Secrecy exists as active global context
British wizarding governance expectations may influence behaviour
Australia is not yet integrated into ICW recognition in this draft model
draftQuestions: Did the stowaway plan to reach Australia, flee Britain, or accidentally arrive?
Does the stowaway possess an official wand/registered wand?
Does any school/Ministry/ICW record know the stowaway exists?

coverOptions: Hidden entirely except for survival interventions
Quietly useful to settlement leadership but not openly magical

firstInvestigationOfIndigenousMagicalSys.recommendedStartingApproach: indirect investigation through signs, tracks, environmental effects, stories, route changes, dreams, failed spells, and protected places before direct practitioner contact
safetyConstraints: Do not invent sacred specifics as canon
Keep restricted knowledge out of Player Mode unless authorised by worldbuilding rules
Use fictionalised systems with clear respect and boundaries
Mark uncertain cultural material as reference/adaptation/draft

misunderstandings: Mistaking land-based magic for wandless magic
Assuming Country can be mapped like British magical territory
Trying to classify ritual practice as charms/wards
Assuming secrecy law is universal in the same form everywhere
Mistaking story/song obligations for folklore rather than law/record/technology
discoveries: Movement through Country follows obligations and knowledge chains
Magic can be relational and place-specific
British spells may behave differently around older local systems

worldFlagsCreatedBySlice.description: Magical presence arrives with or around First Fleet context.
At least one hidden magical outsider is present in 1788 foundation period.
Local magical systems or practitioners detect outsider magic.
Outsider observes local magic but cannot correctly classify it.
Muggle settlement develops under hidden magical observation or intervention.
Early misunderstandings create long-lived tensions and later teaching needs.
Conditions are created for later Australian fusion magic development.
Need for an Australian magical teaching institution begins to emerge.

influences: Crimson Dunes exists because earlier history created a need for local teaching and negotiated magical practice
Waru’s 1810 perspective can inherit warnings, obligations, stories, or consequences from early contact
Outsider groups connected to the emerging school may carry incomplete or biased historical records
ICW recognition pressure soon after 1810 can create institutional stakes
Direct ICW envoy thread can pressure the school to document, classify, and prove itself

openQuestions: Who exactly is the original magical stowaway or hidden magical presence?
Is the first 1788 contact direct or indirect?
What harm, if any, does early misunderstanding cause?
Who preserves the most reliable account of 1788 by 1810?
How much does Waru know or inherit about this period?
